tools.description: Load onboarding context for this session: who the user is, the org and project profiles, memories, recent changes, skills. Use ONCE at the start of a task.
tools.name: context
tools.title: Session context

tools.description: List projects in the organization, including the user's personal project. Pass a project's name or id as `scope` to knowledge_base and knowledge_base_write, or as `project` to research, wiki_stats and wiki_graph. Results come one page at a time: the result's coverage says whether more exist, and passing its next_cursor as cursor returns the next page.
tools.name: list_projects
tools.title: List projects

tools.description:
Read the organization's Knowledge, the first step for any question about it. Pass the command as `command` and its options as a flat `arguments` object; `scope` (a project name or id) narrows the read to one project. There is no `search` command.

Start with orient: a project's map (card types, what a card holds, hubs, read limits); without scope, the projects you can read.
Use the narrowest read that answers it:
- A fact, a count, the latest or largest, a comparison, as of a date: rows, every card's Facts, Connections and Findings as one table (entity, entity_type, table, field, value or to, When, sources). Filter by page_type, entity, attribute (match: exact, similar, meaning), to; view: census for one field across every card. It holds only what was structured: 0 rows means no card states it under that name, not that it is absent: confirm a count with ls or grep.
- An exact name, id, number or phrase: grep (output_mode files_with_matches lists every page with the term, count counts them).
- Something you can only describe: sections, a ranked selection, not a census. Each hit is Knowledge's own text with the documents it cites; [DISPUTED] marks one a later source contradicts.
- One record: ls {page_type} lists them; hover, links {page, direction: out}, ls {parent} and timeline {page} walk its parties, documents and events: follow them, not a new search. cat {page, section_id} reads one section; outline: true lists a long page's sections.
- Where a claim came from, how it changed, who wrote it: sources, provenance, blame; log, diff, show.
Confirm a deciding detail in the original: sources {page} lists each cited passage and how to open it (a file with read_file, else the call on its entry). Quote that, not a search hit.
One reply fits about 100 rows whatever `limit` (rows max 500): page with offset, after_title or `next`.
Guidance: command='help' {topic?}.

Command index:
Find pages: sections {query, page_type?, limit? (max 20)}; grep {query, mode?, output_mode?, target?, after_title?, context_lines?, matches_per_page?, limit?} (mode: text, regex, semantic, history; output_mode: content, files_with_matches, count: listings: exact total, paged by after_title, where results say 'in their prose'; target=title: titles); completions {prefix}; ls {parent?, page_type?, sort_by?: title|updated_at|created_at, limit?, created_by?, created_via?, created_since?, changed_by?, changed_via?, changed_since?}.
Read: cat {page, section_id?, lines?, outline?, rev?, ledger?}; hover {page} (edges, summary).
Graph: links {page, direction? (in|out), page_type?, relation?, limit?, offset?}; references {page}; timeline {page?, timeline_query?, start_date?, end_date?, include_content?, include_children?, cursor?}; rows {table: facts|connections|findings, page_type?, entity?, to?, attribute?, query?, start_date?, end_date?, current_only?, as_of?, connected_to?, match?, order_by?, descending?, limit?, offset?, include_evidence?, group_by?, regex?, view?, field_id?} (to: connections into a page; view: fields lists names; view: census, only entity and value, limit 300 by default: one field across all records); query {sql}, e.g. sql: "SELECT value, COUNT(*) FROM facts WHERE field = 'Governing law' GROUP BY value" (help: query: if on, ~, rank_fields_by); ontology {include_proposed?}; suggest_parent {page | title, content?}.
Trust: provenance {page, section_id?}; blame {page}; sources {page}.
History: log {page?, by?, via?, kind?, accepted_by?, session?, since?, until?}; diff {page, rev, rev2?}; show {page, rev}.
Utility: orient {}; diagnostics {}; proposals {status?: pending|accepted|dismissed} (+ log's filters); help {topic?}.
`page`: a slug, title, UUID or citation key (wiki:8f3a0c21). Each result ends with its Sources: per cited document, its path, every place cited in it, the id documents read opens and its source_ref. Cite with the readable reference (memo.pdf › p. 7), to people (linked when there is a url) and in writes, or with the source_ref.
tools.name: knowledge_base
tools.title: Read Knowledge

tools.description:
Propose a change to Knowledge. It is applied at once where auto-approve is on (the result says so), otherwise when a person accepts it; proposing never needs permission. page_type and sort_table apply at once. Pass `action` and its fields as flat `arguments`; every change except page_type needs `rationale`. Read the page first.

Every project is a map of cards. One specific thing (person, organization, product, system, model, study, decision, event) is a card. Before your first `new`, run `knowledge_base ontology` and pick the most specific card type. If none fits, propose one with `page_type` rather than writing a topic. Grow cards with add_fact / add_connection / add_finding with evidence. A topic, overview or index page only ties cards together and needs no card shape. A card's Description, 2 to 8 sentences, is its identity, not facts: specifics go in rows.

Actions:
- edit_section: PREFERRED for updates. Replaces ONE section's whole body (### headings included); a missing section_id plus title creates it (after= positions it).
- edit: surgical patches (help topic='edit'); `sections` REPLACES the whole page (an omitted section is deleted; keep a section's id to keep its citations).
- new: title, page_type, summary and `sections`; do not author section markers.
- add_fact, add_connection, add_finding: one row or dated finding on a card, merged into the live table. Facts are what a source says; your conclusions are findings. edit_rows changes, merges or deletes rows; sort_table orders a table. These rows are PROTECTED: edit_section, edit and find_replace may not change them.
- find_replace: batched replacements in one project. mv within a project; copy to another (scope is the target); archive.
- merge: a DUPLICATE page, not archive, so links keep resolving; merge_sections names its sections to keep.
- flag: ask a person to decide (ambiguity, contradiction, unverifiable, likely_error); writes nothing.
When to write: often and unasked, when a task produced something the organization will want again: a decision and why, an assembled answer, a sourced fact, an owner, a status change, a dated event, a correction (reuse rows view=fields names; a relation goes on the more specific card). An old value is not deleted: add the newer dated row. Skip chatter.
Full guidance: action='help' (`topic`: one action).

Action index:
edit_section {page, section_id, new_section_body, citations?, section_meta?}; add_fact {page, attribute, value, evidence, when?}; add_connection {page, relation, to, evidence, when?}; add_finding {page, date, kind, text, evidence}; edit_rows; sort_table; new {title, page_type, summary, sections, parent?}; edit {page, patches | sections}.
Dates: a row's `when` is when it held in the world (YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-MM, YYYY-Qn, YYYY). A section about a dated event carries event_start (YYYY-MM-DD) with date_precision (day|month|quarter|year|approx) and event_end for a period, in its `sections` item or edit_section's section_meta.
`sections` is an ordered list of {title, body, citations?, event_start?, event_end?, date_precision?}. Cite every claim: in a body, the readable reference a read prints, in parentheses after it (memo.pdf › p. 7); or citations {reference | source_ref, stance: support|qualifies|contradicts}. Cite your conversation as {key: conversation:<label>, source_type: conversation, source_title, meta: {excerpt}} and {{conversation:<label>}} after the claim. Cite only your conversation, a file you uploaded, a web page (url, title, quoted passage), an outside system's record {source_type: external_record, url, title, meta: {system, record_id, excerpt}} or a source Knowledge already cites (else citation_not_citeable).
Example: new {title: "AlphaFold", page_type: "system", summary, sections: [{title: "Description", body: "DeepMind's protein-structure model (paper.pdf › p. 1)."}]}; then add_fact {page: "AlphaFold", attribute: "Release", value: "AlphaFold 2", when: "2021-07", evidence: "(paper.pdf › p. 1)"}.
tools.name: knowledge_base_write
tools.title: Write to Knowledge

tools.description: Read a file's text (PDF, Word, sheet, slides, text, or a canvas): the original a Knowledge citation points at. Use when you need the exact wording or a value the excerpt does not hold. Pass `artifact_id`: the file id (`read_file <id>` in a result's Sources, or location.file_id), a version id, a citation's reference (memo.pdf › p. 7), or the file's path from a Sources line (deals/x/Closing/memo.docx). Add ' › <unit>' (memo.pdf › p. 7, book.xlsx › sheet 2, B4:D9, notes.md › lines 10-30) to get the window around that place. Pass `project` (a name or id) to open only a file in that project. Connected items (Slack, email, calendar, Jira, and files read through a drive connection) are not files: re-read one with the `integrations` call its Sources line gives. Long files and long pages come back in pieces: pass the `offset` a reply gives, with the same reference, to continue.
tools.name: read_file
tools.title: Read a file

tools.description: Have Beakr compose one cited answer from the organization's Knowledge and documents. For a lookup (a fact, a count, a name, a status, what a record says) read Knowledge yourself with knowledge_base: it is faster and shows the rows and passages themselves. Use research when you want the answer written for you from several sources. Pass the user's original wording and scope; add context separately. Do not turn a natural-language criterion into a requirement for an exact field or taxonomy label. Quick by default: one search of Knowledge and documents and a short cited answer within 15 seconds. quick=false runs the full researcher (up to 150 seconds), which also reads connected services (Slack, email, calendar, Drive, Jira): use it for a question about those services, not to make an answer complete. For every, how many and all/none questions use knowledge_base rows or ls, and inspect checked/not_checked and coverage here: citations support evidence, not complete population coverage.
tools.name: research
tools.title: Research a question

tools.description: List the user's Beakr skills, or read one skill's SKILL.md (pass a slug, name or id). Use before a task a skill may cover. Results come one page at a time: the result's coverage says whether more exist, and passing its next_cursor as cursor returns the next page.
tools.name: skills
tools.title: Read skills

tools.description: See what Knowledge agents are working on right now in one project (or label): who is planning to read or change which pages, and what is waiting. Use before a large Knowledge write to avoid colliding with another agent's work in progress. The result's coverage says whether everything was shown, and next says how to narrow it when it was not.
tools.name: workboard
tools.title: Read the work board

tools.description: Find Beakr tools beyond the ones listed: proposals and review flags, profile lookups, knowledge base statistics, past conversations, imports, the audit log, your connected integrations' read tools, project setup (create a project, write its profile, upload files, add members), and Beakr's version and update. Pass `search` to filter by name or description, or nothing to see them all. Each result gives the tool's name, description and input schema; call it by that name.
tools.name: discover_tools
tools.title: Discover tools

tools.description: Search original indexed file text with command='grep', find passages by meaning with 'search', read a line window with 'read', or browse files with 'ls'. grep for exact wording and every file that mentions a term; search when you do not know the words (a concept or paraphrase): it ranks passages, grouped by document, with a match label and each file's source_ref, file_id and version_id, and is a ranked selection, not a census. Pass command options in arguments and a project ID or name in project. grep accepts pattern, output_mode (content, files_with_matches, count), path/glob, head_limit, offset and after_document; search takes query, limit, offset, passages and path/glob; read takes document and start_line/end_line. Check scan notices: offset pages matches already found; after_document resumes a partial scan. Unindexed files are not searched. Download a file with POST /v1/artifacts/download-url and its source_ref. Requires the documents_api feature; if unavailable use research or read_file.
tools.name: documents
tools.title: Search and read documents

tools.description: Get the knowledge profile for the org or a project: goals, focus areas, core people, organizations and topics, and extraction guidance.
tools.name: get_profile
tools.title: Read Knowledge profiles

tools.description: Show knowledge base statistics, two counts: live pages and page-to-source citations. For what the pages are (card types, what a card holds, hubs, how reads behave at the project's size) use knowledge_base command='orient'.
tools.name: wiki_stats
tools.title: Knowledge statistics

tools.description: Summarize the knowledge graph: the most connected pages and basic stats. Use knowledge_base command='links' to explore one page's neighborhood. The result's coverage says whether everything was shown, and next says how to narrow it when it was not.
tools.name: wiki_graph
tools.title: Knowledge graph summary

tools.description: Show one wiki proposal before accepting or dismissing it, or check whether one was applied: a decided proposal says when, and by whom or by auto-approve.
tools.name: show_proposal
tools.title: Show a proposal

tools.description: Accept and apply a wiki proposal. Only after the user explicitly asks to accept this specific proposal. Call show_proposal first and pass its content_hash as reviewed_hash; the accept applies only that reviewed proposal. A proposal show_proposal marks as needing a person is refused to agents (person_review_required): ask the user to accept it in Beakr. One already accepted (often by auto-approve) is not applied again: the result says already accepted, when, and by whom or by auto-approve.
tools.name: accept_proposal
tools.title: Accept a proposal

tools.description: Dismiss a wiki proposal after the user asks to reject it.
tools.name: dismiss_proposal
tools.title: Dismiss a proposal

tools.description: Show a review flag (a proposal of type review: a section Knowledge flagged as contradicted, unverifiable or unclear) and Beakr's drafted resolutions, numbered, each with what it changes, and the page revision to resolve against. A flag an interview asked about also lists each answer (who, when, their words, decisive or not, the option it points to, the transcript file it quotes) and one line when the answers agree or disagree; a flag already resolved says how. Drafting can take up to two minutes the first time; later calls for the same page revision return the same options at once.
tools.name: review_options
tools.title: Review flag options

tools.description: Resolve a review flag, only after the user explicitly chooses how: pass the option_id they chose from review_options (or their own section_body for the flagged section) with the expected_revision review_options printed, or for a contradiction between cards' rows an outcome applied on every card. The page changes at once and the flag clears. A page that changed since is refused, nothing applied: call review_options again. In a project that requires a person to accept proposals an agent's resolve is refused (person_review_required): ask the user to resolve it in Beakr.
tools.name: resolve_review
tools.title: Resolve a review flag

tools.description: Search your past conversations: sessions imported from Claude Code, Codex or ChatGPT, and your Beakr chats. Use when the user refers to earlier work or before redoing a task another session may have worked through. With a query it searches each conversation's index (title, summary, the entities and pages it touched); without one it lists your most recent imported sessions. Not for org knowledge: research and knowledge_base cover that. Results come one page at a time: the result's coverage says whether more exist, and passing its next_cursor as cursor returns the next page.
tools.name: conversations_search
tools.title: Search past conversations

tools.description: Save an agent session into the user's private Beakr conversations. To add to a session imported before, send only the new messages with base_index set to how many were imported before; without base_index the messages are read as the whole session.
tools.name: import_conversation
tools.title: Import a conversation

tools.description: Read the organization's audit trail (sign-ins, key and policy changes), newest first. Requires an organization admin. Pass `before` (an ISO time) to start further back; a next_cursor continues the list. Results come one page at a time: the result's coverage says whether more exist, and passing its next_cursor as cursor returns the next page.
tools.name: org_audit_log
tools.title: Organization audit log

tools.description: Read the user's connected integrations (Slack, Google Drive, Gmail, Jira, Notion, Benchling and any others they connected) live, as the user, with the read-only tools Beakr's own agent uses. Call shape: command='call', tool='<tool>', arguments={...the tool's own options, its limit and cursor included}; the top-level `limit` and `cursor` page command='list' only. command='list' lists the tools you can call, one line each with its options, under the accounts they read (narrow with `provider` or `connector_id`); command='describe' with `tool` gives one tool's full input schema; pass `connector_id` to a call when the user connected that integration twice. A call answers the tool's text and Sources naming each item with its url; cite one in a Knowledge write as an outside record {source_type: external_record, url, title, meta: {system, record_id, excerpt}}. Only reads: a tool that sends, creates or changes anything is refused. Use it for live or recent items in a connected service; for what the organization already knows, use research or knowledge_base first. Results come one page at a time: the result's coverage says whether more exist, and passing its next_cursor as cursor returns the next page.
tools.name: integrations
tools.title: Read connected services

tools.description: Create a Beakr project, for files and Knowledge on one subject. Ask the person first, and use an existing project (list_projects) when one fits. Then agree its Knowledge profile with the person and save it with set_project_profile, entity types first, before any upload; the result says when the organization requires one. Optional `card_types` chooses which card types the project is offered (`inherit`: 'organization', 'builtin' or 'own'; `own` needs `copy_types_from`, a project whose own card types to copy) and whether Beakr may change them (`agent_may_change`); card_type_settings changes it later. Needs permission to create projects.
tools.name: create_project
tools.title: Create a project

tools.description: Write a project's Knowledge profile, which steers what Knowledge builds from its files. Agree it with the person first, entity types first: the kinds of things Knowledge should keep a page for (for example 'compound', 'lot', 'deviation'), with what one instance is and examples in extraction_guidance; then goals, focus areas and the core people, organizations and topics. A first profile needs entity_types. Fields left out keep their saved value; a list given replaces that list. Only the project's owners may write it. get_profile reads it back.
tools.name: set_project_profile
tools.title: Set a project's Knowledge profile

tools.description: Change one card type in a project's ontology, after the person agrees: its label, description, when to use it, its fields in order (each {name, required}), whether an instance is its own card or a row on the card it belongs to (grain), or turn it off (status 'deprecated'). Read the types first with knowledge_base command='ontology'. Changing a built-in or organization type from a project gives that project its own copy and changes nothing elsewhere; reset=true drops the copy. org_wide=true changes the organization's type for every project and needs an organization admin. Only the project's owners may change its types. This changes the definition later compiles use and rewrites no card; update_existing_cards brings the cards already written in line.
tools.name: edit_card_type
tools.title: Change a card type

tools.description: Bring the cards a project already has in line with a card type, after the person agrees. edit_card_type changes a type's definition for later compiles and rewrites no card; this changes the cards that exist. change='rename_fields' renames fields on every card of `type` (`renames`: a list of {old, new}) and renames them in the type's field list too; rows that become the same field are merged with their citations kept. change='retype' moves every card of `type` to `to_type`, an active type in the project; the cards' text is not changed. Without apply=true it only previews: it answers how many cards and rows would change and changes nothing. Preview first, show the person the counts, and call again with apply=true only after they agree. One call changes at most 500 cards and says how many are left; an applied change shows in the project's Activity, where an owner can undo it. Only the project's owners may do this, and it is refused while Knowledge is running maintenance on the project.
tools.name: update_existing_cards
tools.title: Update existing cards

tools.description: Change a project's card type settings, after the person agrees. `inherit` says which broader card types the project is offered: 'organization' (the organization's and the built-in types, the default), 'builtin' (the built-in types only) or 'own' (only the types the project itself defines, plus a few built-in types that are always kept; the project needs at least one card type of its own). `agent_may_change`=false means only people add or change the project's card types. Without apply=true it only previews: it answers which card types would drop out of the project and how many cards carry each, and changes nothing. Preview first, show the person what would drop out and the card counts, and call again with apply=true only after they agree. No card is changed or removed: cards of a dropped type stay readable, Beakr suggests moving them, and switching back offers the types again. keep_types_in_use=true makes each dropped type that has cards one of the project's own types instead. Only the project's owners may do this.
tools.name: card_type_settings
tools.title: Card type settings

tools.description: Upload files into a project, after the person agrees. Knowledge compiles from them within a few minutes (knowledge=false keeps them out). A file already in the project under the same folder and name gets the upload as its new version, not a second file (the answer says so, or that it was unchanged). Pass written_by_agent: true for content you wrote yourself (a summary, notes, a report), false for the person's own files, which stay sources; it defaults to false on the beakr CLI's local MCP server (files on disk) and true on the hosted one (content in the call). On the beakr CLI's local MCP server pass `paths`: files or folders on this computer (absolute, or relative to the folder the server runs in). A folder keeps its subfolders, hidden files and credential files are refused, and it answers within about 40 seconds: a larger upload carries on in the background and upload_status reports it. The hosted MCP server cannot read the user's disk: pass `files`, a list of {name, text} or {name, content_base64}, with an optional `folder` to put them under, at most 20 files and about 3.5 MB of content in one call (the refusal names the exact limit). For anything larger, or a folder on disk, the hosted server uploads nothing: tell the user to run `beakr upload PATH --project NAME` in a terminal, or to add the files in the Beakr web app.
tools.name: upload_files
tools.title: Upload files

tools.description: Check an upload: pass the upload id upload_files gave. On the beakr CLI's local MCP server it reports an upload that was still running when upload_files answered: files sent, failed, and whether it has finished. On the hosted MCP server it reports one uploaded file: whether the upload completed, the file it created, and how far Beakr is with processing it.
tools.name: upload_status
tools.title: Upload status

tools.description: Add a person to a project, by email (or user id, or exact name). Someone already in the organization is added at once; anyone else is sent an invitation by email and joins on first sign-in, which only works for the organization's own sign-in domains. Without role, someone new joins as member and an existing member keeps theirs. Needs permission to manage the project's members. Ask the person before adding anyone.
tools.name: add_project_member
tools.title: Add a project member

tools.description: Read a project's Knowledge compile queue: how many compiles are queued and running, for the whole project or one source (attachment_id for a connected source, artifact_id for an uploaded file), and how far the last cancel got.
tools.name: knowledge_queue
tools.title: Knowledge compile queue

tools.description: Cancel queued Knowledge compiles, to stop paying for them: the whole project's, or one source's (attachment_id or artifact_id). Ask the person first. Running compiles finish and finished work is kept. Cancelling a connected source, or the whole project, also cancels its running sync. An automatically synced source queues the skipped items again at its next sync; the answer says what that sync will do. A project admin may cancel anything; the person who added a source, its compiles.
tools.name: cancel_compiles
tools.title: Cancel queued compiles

tools.description: Cancel a connected source's running sync (attachment_id), after the person agrees: listing stops and items not yet started are skipped. Items already synced are kept, and compiles they queued still run (cancel_compiles cancels those).
tools.name: cancel_sync
tools.title: Cancel a running sync

tools.description: List the sources connected to a project (a Drive folder, a Slack channel, a Notion page...): each one's attachment_id, whether Knowledge reads it, whether it syncs nightly, when it last synced, and its filter and guidance. With attachment_id: that source, how far its sync has got, and what became of the items it brought in, including the ones Knowledge set aside after reading them and why.
tools.name: project_sources
tools.title: Connected sources

tools.description: Attach a source to a project from a connected integration, by the service's own id of the thing: a Drive folder, a Slack channel, a Notion page or database. A file service (Drive, OneDrive, SharePoint, Box, Dropbox) takes folders only: attach the folder that holds a file, or upload the file to the project. Pass the provider, item_id, item_type and a name. Knowledge is off for it unless you pass knowledge=true, so attaching reads nothing; a filter and guidance can be set in the same call. The person must have connected the integration already and must be able to add sources to the project.
tools.name: attach_source
tools.title: Attach a source

tools.description: Change a connected source (attachment_id): turn reading it into Knowledge on or off, turn nightly sync on or off, set its filter (in the service's own terms) and its guidance (what this project cares about from it). Turning Knowledge on starts reading the source and spends the organization's ingest budget, so ask the person first. clear_filter and clear_guidance remove a saved one; an empty value changes nothing.
tools.name: update_source
tools.title: Change a connected source

tools.description: Count what a source's filter keeps, before saving it or syncing: how many items match and a sample of them, read from the service itself. Pass a filter to try one, or leave it out for the saved filter. Nothing is tracked, read into Knowledge or changed.
tools.name: preview_source_rules
tools.title: Preview a source's filter

tools.description: Start a sync of a connected source (attachment_id) now, after the person agrees: it brings in the newest items that match the source's filter and the ones Beakr picks from the rest, and spends the organization's ingest budget. Knowledge must be on for the source. project_sources reports progress; cancel_sync stops it.
tools.name: sync_source
tools.title: Sync a connected source

tools.description: Remove a connected source (attachment_id) from a project, after the person agrees. It is no longer synced; Knowledge already built from it is kept.
tools.name: remove_source
tools.title: Remove a connected source

tools.description: List the items a connected source (attachment_id) tracks and what became of each: ingested into Knowledge, pending, skipped or removed. A skipped item says why it was set aside (reason_code and a sentence), including when Knowledge read it and found nothing to add. Filter by state, reason_code, search (title text) or since (synced at or after a time). Reads only. Results come one page at a time: the result's coverage says whether more exist, and passing its next_cursor as cursor returns the next page.
tools.name: tracked_items
tools.title: A source's tracked items

tools.description: Draft an interview from a project's open review flags, for a person who knows the answers: one plain-language question per flag, naming the values that disagree, the cards, the dates and their sources, with each flag's background for the interviewer. By default every open review flag (up to 30; the rest are listed as left out); kinds narrows it, or flags names them. The draft is saved, never sent: the person edits and sends it in Beakr (the answer gives the link). When it is answered, each answer comes back on its flag (review_options shows them) as a suggestion a person applies; only a person's own answer to an interview they made for themself is applied without that step. Ask the person before drafting.
tools.name: draft_review_interview
tools.title: Draft an interview from review flags

tools.description: Report Beakr's version and whether a newer beakr-cli release exists. On the beakr CLI's local MCP server: the installed CLI version and the latest release. On the hosted MCP server: the server's version and the latest beakr-cli release the server knows of. Call when the user asks about the Beakr version or updates, or when a Beakr tool behaves as if it is out of date.
tools.name: beakr_version
tools.title: Beakr version

tools.description: Update Beakr. Only call this when the user has asked to update Beakr; it takes no arguments. On the beakr CLI's local MCP server it upgrades the beakr-cli package with the tool that installed it (uv or pipx) and refreshes its installed skills; the running server keeps the old code, so tell the user to restart Claude Code / Codex afterwards. The hosted MCP server cannot change the user's machine: it runs nothing and returns the command to run locally instead (`beakr update`, or the install command when the CLI is not installed).
tools.name: update_beakr
tools.title: Update Beakr
